## Overview
On ROCm, DCP's query all-gather runs through RCCL. This PR routes it through AITER's custom all-gather, which has already existed in vLLM's AITER custom collectives, through a dedicated communicator instance for the aiter DCP group.


## Claims
- On Kimi-K3, MI355X x8 with TP8 and DCP8, using AITER's all-gather achieves ~1% - ~4% output throughput across concurrency
- The aiter gathered query is identical to gathering through the RCCL path, and end-to-end accuracy is unchanged.
- Settings with DCP disabled are unaffected


## Validation

Unit tests matching AITER query gather with using RCCL

SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --moe-backend auto \
  --load-format auto \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --language-model-only \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k3
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>lm_eval command</summary>

```
lm-eval run --model local-chat-completions --model_args "model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,max_gen_toks=8192,timeout=3600" --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --seed 1234
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>benchmark command</summary>

```
vllm bench serve --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --backend vllm --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency "$CONC" --num-prompts $((CONC * 4)) --temperature 0 --ignore-eos
```

</details>



## Details

When DCP is enabled, each MLA layer gathers the decode query across ranks in the DCP group before attention. On ROCm, it currently goes through RCCL, and since RCCL concatenates along dim 0, this path requires copying results so that the head ordering is correct. AITER's all-gather gathers along the last dimension, so gathering a query viewed as `[T, H * D]` is exactly gathering along the heads, and it's able to write into the final layout with no reordering copy. Measuring on Kimi-K3 with TP8 and DCP8, this decreases per-layer gather latency from RCCL path's 31.9us to AITER path's 16.2us in decode traces.

The is enabled for ROCm and only in single-node DCP settings when AITER custom all-reduce is enabled. When its requirements are not met, this gather falls back to using RCCL.

@kliuae  it's a minor thing, so you can skip this. This may help to reduce memory (or increase kv cache size) by not allocating IPC buffers when TP=DCP. 

### Suggestion: reuse TP's AITER instance when the DCP group equals the TP group

When `decode_context_parallel_size == tensor_parallel_size` and PCP is 1, the DCP group contains the same ranks as TP, in the same order (`parallel_state.py`: DCP spans PCP, then TP). TP already has an `aiter_ar_comm` on ROCm by default. So the extra DCP instance only adds a second set of IPC buffers, and on Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 that costs about 0.36 GiB of KV cache per rank. Reusing TP's instance also removes the need for the `graph_capture` change in this case, because TP's capture already enters it. Configs where the DCP ranks differ from TP (DCP < TP, or PCP > 1) still build the dedicated DCP instance, exactly as this PR does now.

<details>
<summary>diff on top of this PR (4bc0ae35)</summary>

```diff
--- a/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/cuda_communicator.py
+++ b/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/cuda_communicator.py
@@ -175,10 +175,12 @@
-        # AITER all-gather for the MLA DCP query gather
+        # AITER all-gather for the MLA DCP query gather. When DCP spans the TP
+        # group, the gather reuses TP's instance (see MLADCPManager).
         if (
             unique_name.split(":")[0] == "dcp"
             and self.aiter_ar_comm is None
+            and not _dcp_matches_tp(self.ranks)
             and self.world_size in (2, 4, 8)
@@
+
+
+def _dcp_matches_tp(ranks: list[int]) -> bool:
+    from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import _TP
+
+    return _TP is not None and list(_TP.ranks) == list(ranks)
--- a/vllm/v1/attention/ops/dcp.py
+++ b/vllm/v1/attention/ops/dcp.py
@@ -1589,6 +1589,12 @@
         aiter_comm = getattr(self.group.device_communicator, "aiter_ar_comm", None)
+        if aiter_comm is None:
+            from vllm.distributed import get_tp_group
+
+            tp_group = get_tp_group()
+            if tp_group.ranks == self.group.ranks:
+                aiter_comm = getattr(tp_group.device_communicator, "aiter_ar_comm", None)
         if aiter_comm is not None:
```

</details>

### Results

Setup: Kimi-K3 on MI355X x8, TP8/DCP8, `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-77154ca6`. The serve flags match the PR description, except that prefix caching is disabled. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve`, random 8192/1024, `num_prompts = 4 x conc`, run after a warmup pass. One run per arm.

| | main | this PR | this PR + TP reuse |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU KV cache size | 33,896,102 tokens | 33,684,031 (-0.63%) | **33,978,575** (+0.24%) |
| Output tok/s, conc 16 | 569.65 | 587.95 (+3.2%) | 587.48 (+3.1%) |
| Output tok/s, conc 32 | 868.42 | 893.95 (+2.9%) | 891.68 (+2.7%) |
| Output tok/s, conc 64 | 1,189.90 | 1,212.22 (+1.9%) | 1,213.71 (+2.0%) |
| Output tok/s, conc 128 | 1,474.56 | 1,493.83 (+1.3%) | 1,490.85 (+1.1%) |
| Mean TPOT, conc 16 / 128 (ms) | 26.09 / 78.85 | 25.23 / 77.78 | 25.25 / 77.94 |
| gsm8k 20-shot, flexible / strict | 0.9682 / 0.9682 | 0.9636 / 0.9644 | 0.9666 / 0.9674 |

- **Memory:** with TP reuse, the KV cache goes back to main's level. This PR alone loses about 212k tokens, roughly 0.36 GiB per rank.
- **Performance:** the TP-reuse variant is within ±0.3% of this PR at every concurrency, so it keeps the gather speedup. TTFT is flat across all three arms.
- **Accuracy:** gsm8k differences between all three arms are within about 1 stderr (±0.005).
- **Correctness:** `test_distributed_aiter_q_gather_matches_rccl` (bf16 and fp8, including CUDA graph replay) passes with the TP-reuse variant. For that run the test was adapted to assert that the DCP communicator has no instance of its own and to use TP's instead.

Not covered here: DCP < TP (e.g. TP8/DCP4), which should take the dedicated-instance path unchanged.

Thanks for your suggestion and detailed measurements. Initially we considered this path too, but due to its limit to TP==DCP settings and the concern of potential simultaneous use of the same IPC buffer if AR and AG happen to be put on different streams (though it doesn't happen in today's vllm), we opted for a separate instance for DCP.

@kliuae @hongxiayang @tjtanaa 
Before you merge this pr, we will do some stress test with agentx workload and will share the results. We found some deadlock and need to check if it is from this aiter ag or not.

The hang only happened on a specific node and was not visible on other nodes on agentx benchmark & stress tests too. 

Looks good 

**Update (2026-10-18): the hang is node-specific and does not reproduce with this PR on other nodes.** Both hangs happened on one node (pit2-p03-g10). On two other MI355X nodes, the same image, recipe and PR ran clean for several hours, with the same throughput as without the PR. We no longer attribute the hang to this PR. The original report is kept below for reference.

**Results (all c60 / max-num-seqs 120, same image, recipe and PR commit)**

| node | PR | run | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| g10 | yes | c60 try 1 | hang, about 11 min into the measured run |
| g10 | yes | c60 try 2 | hang, about 46 min into the measured run |
| g03 | no | c60 control | clean, 15,388 tok/s/GPU |
| g03 | yes | 4 back-to-back c60 passes against one server (about 6 h, 4 h measured) | clean, no hang |
| g09 | yes | c60 run 1 | clean, 15,345 tok/s/GPU, 8 / 3,702 request errors |
| g09 | yes | c60 run 2 | clean, 15,353 tok/s/GPU, 7 / 3,710 request errors |

- The PR has no measurable throughput effect: 15,345 / 15,353 tok/s/GPU with the PR on g09 vs 15,388 without it on g03.
- TTFT, TPOT and interactivity are within run-to-run noise.

<details>
<summary>Original report (2026-10-17), superseded by the update above</summary>

Stress test results with the AgentX workload: with this PR we see a reproducible all-rank hang at higher concurrency. The same setup without the PR runs clean.

**Setup**
- MI355X x8, Kimi-K3 FP4, TP8 / DCP8, `dcp_comm_backend=a2a`, DSpark spec decode (4 tokens, synthetic acceptance length 3.36)
- `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (CPU KV offload), `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraphs, `max-num-batched-tokens 8192`
- `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=0`, so the query gather goes through this PR's path (log: `Using AITER custom all-gather for the MLA DCP query.`)
- Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294` (aiter 0.1.25), PR applied at `8033f2c`
- AgentX trace replay (`semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`), 1 h measured run after warmup

**Hang signature on g10** (identical on both tries)
- Engine throughput drops to 0 with about 55–60 running requests, while CPU-offload KV loads are in flight.
- About 600 s later, every rank (0–7) times out on the same NCCL all-gather:
  ```
  Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=21277, OpType=_ALLGATHER_BASE, NumelIn=5529600, NumelOut=44236800, Timeout(ms)=600000)
  ```
  (try 1: `SeqNum=326677, NumelIn=4755456`)
- `NumelIn` is exactly `num_tokens x 12 heads x 576` (800 and 688 tokens), which matches the DCP query gather. In bf16 that is above the `should_custom_ag` limit (8 MiB per rank, about 606 tokens), so it is this PR's NCCL fallback inside `_aiter_query_gather`.

**Possible mechanism (hypothesis, not confirmed)**
- With the PR, the DCP group alternates between AITER `allgather_lastdim` (small batches, cudagraph decode) and NCCL `all_gather` (large mixed-prefill batches).
- One rank's GPU stream may have been blocked by an earlier AITER custom kernel still spinning in `start_sync`/`end_sync`. For reference, ROCm/aiter#4786 (open) changes the cross-device flag loads in `start_sync`/`end_sync` from `DEVICE` to `SYSTEM` scope. aiter 0.1.25 in this image still uses `DEVICE`.

**Review note:** the DCP direct workspaces are allocated per ubatch (`num_ubatches`), but the new AITER instance on the DCP group (one signal buffer, one staging buffer) is shared. With ubatch overlap enabled, two concurrent query gathers could use the same instance. That was not enabled in our runs.

</details>

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

- On Kimi-K3, MI355X x8 with TP8 and DCP8, using AITER's all-gather achieves ~1% - ~4% output throughput across concurrency
- The aiter gathered query is identical to gathering through the RCCL path, and end-to-end accuracy is unchanged.
- Settings with DCP disabled are unaffected


## Validation

```

</details>



## Details

When DCP is enabled, each MLA layer gathers the decode query across ranks in the DCP group before attention. On ROCm, it currently goes through RCCL, and since RCCL concatenates along dim 0, this path requires copying results so that the head ordering is correct. AITER's all-gather gathers along the last dimension, so gathering a query viewed as `[T, H * D]` is exactly gathering along the heads, and it's able to write into the final layout with no reordering copy. Measuring on Kimi-K3 with TP8 and DCP8, this decreases per-layer gather latency from RCCL path's 31.9us to AITER path's 16.2us in decode traces.

The is enabled for ROCm and only in single-node DCP settings when AITER custom all-reduce is enabled. When its requirements are not met, this gather falls back to using RCCL.

+def _distributed_aiter_q_gather_worker(env: dict[str, str]) -> None:
+    update_environment_variables(env)
+    local_rank = int(env["LOCAL_RANK"])
+    world_size = int(env["WORLD_SIZE"])
+    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{local_rank}")
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(local_rank)
+    from vllm.config import ParallelConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.distributed import cleanup_dist_env_and_memory
+    from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import (
+        get_dcp_group,
+        graph_capture,
+        init_distributed_environment,
+        initialize_model_parallel,
+    )
+
+    config = VllmConfig(
+        parallel_config=ParallelConfig(
+            tensor_parallel_size=world_size, decode_context_parallel_size=world_size
+        )
+    )
+    with set_current_vllm_config(config):
+        init_distributed_environment()
+        initialize_model_parallel(
+            tensor_model_parallel_size=world_size,
+            decode_context_model_parallel_size=world_size,
+        )
+        try:
+            rank = dist.get_rank()
+            dcp_comm = get_dcp_group().device_communicator
+            aiter_comm = dcp_comm.aiter_ar_comm
+            assert aiter_comm is not None
+            # DCP all-reduces must not route to the gather's AITER instance.
+            assert not dcp_comm.use_aiter_allreduce
+            dtype = _dtype_from_name(env["TEST_DTYPE"])
+            # Kimi-K3 at TP8: 12 local heads of kv_lora 512 + rope 64, padded to 128.
+            heads_per_rank, head_dim, padded_num_heads = 12, 576, 128
+            manager = MagicMock(padded_num_heads=padded_num_heads)
+            manager._gather_query = MagicMock(side_effect=AssertionError("fell back"))
+
+            def expected_bytes(local_query: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+                # Compare bytes: RCCL has no fp8 all-gather.
+                local_bytes = local_query.view(torch.uint8)
+                gathered = [torch.empty_like(local_bytes) for _ in range(world_size)]
+                dist.all_gather(gathered, local_bytes)
+                return torch.cat(gathered, dim=1)
+
+            def random_query(num_tokens: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+                return torch.randn(
+                    num_tokens, heads_per_rank, head_dim, device=device
+                ).to(dtype)
+
+            for num_tokens in (1, 7, 160):
+                local_query = random_query(num_tokens)
+                actual = dcp.MLADCPManager._aiter_query_gather(
+                    manager, aiter_comm, local_query
+                )
+                expected = expected_bytes(local_query)
+                assert actual.dtype == dtype
+                assert actual.view(torch.uint8).shape == expected.shape
+                assert actual.untyped_storage().nbytes() >= (
+                    num_tokens * padded_num_heads * head_dim * actual.element_size()
+                )
+                assert torch.equal(actual.view(torch.uint8), expected), (
+                    f"rank {rank} tokens {num_tokens}"
+                )
+
+            # vLLM's graph capture puts the DCP instance in capture mode, so the
+            # captured gather reads the query from registered graph buffers.
+            static_query = random_query(7)
+            with graph_capture(device) as capture_context:
+                graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+                with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=capture_context.stream):
+                    captured = dcp.MLADCPManager._aiter_query_gather(
+                        manager, aiter_comm, static_query
+                    )
+            for replay in range(2):
+                local_query = random_query(7)
+                static_query.copy_(local_query)
+                graph.replay()
+                assert torch.equal(
+                    captured.view(torch.uint8), expected_bytes(local_query)
+                ), f"rank {rank} replay {replay}"
+        finally:
+            cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()
+
+

@kliuae  it's a minor thing, so you can skip this. This may help to reduce memory (or increase kv cache size) by not allocating IPC buffers when TP=DCP. 

### Suggestion: reuse TP's AITER instance when the DCP group equals the TP group

When `decode_context_parallel_size == tensor_parallel_size` and PCP is 1, the DCP group contains the same ranks as TP, in the same order (`parallel_state.py`: DCP spans PCP, then TP). TP already has an `aiter_ar_comm` on ROCm by default. So the extra DCP instance only adds a second set of IPC buffers, and on Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 that costs about 0.36 GiB of KV cache per rank. Reusing TP's instance also removes the need for the `graph_capture` change in this case, because TP's capture already enters it. Configs where the DCP ranks differ from TP (DCP < TP, or PCP > 1) still build the dedicated DCP instance, exactly as this PR does now.

### Results

Setup: Kimi-K3 on MI355X x8, TP8/DCP8, `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-77154ca6`. The serve flags match the PR description, except that prefix caching is disabled. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve`, random 8192/1024, `num_prompts = 4 x conc`, run after a warmup pass. One run per arm.

| | main | this PR | this PR + TP reuse |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU KV cache size | 33,896,102 tokens | 33,684,031 (-0.63%) | **33,978,575** (+0.24%) |
| Output tok/s, conc 16 | 569.65 | 587.95 (+3.2%) | 587.48 (+3.1%) |
| Output tok/s, conc 32 | 868.42 | 893.95 (+2.9%) | 891.68 (+2.7%) |
| Output tok/s, conc 64 | 1,189.90 | 1,212.22 (+1.9%) | 1,213.71 (+2.0%) |
| Output tok/s, conc 128 | 1,474.56 | 1,493.83 (+1.3%) | 1,490.85 (+1.1%) |
| Mean TPOT, conc 16 / 128 (ms) | 26.09 / 78.85 | 25.23 / 77.78 | 25.25 / 77.94 |
| gsm8k 20-shot, flexible / strict | 0.9682 / 0.9682 | 0.9636 / 0.9644 | 0.9666 / 0.9674 |

- **Memory:** with TP reuse, the KV cache goes back to main's level. This PR alone loses about 212k tokens, roughly 0.36 GiB per rank.
- **Performance:** the TP-reuse variant is within ±0.3% of this PR at every concurrency, so it keeps the gather speedup. TTFT is flat across all three arms.
- **Accuracy:** gsm8k differences between all three arms are within about 1 stderr (±0.005).
- **Correctness:** `test_distributed_aiter_q_gather_matches_rccl` (bf16 and fp8, including CUDA graph replay) passes with the TP-reuse variant. For that run the test was adapted to assert that the DCP communicator has no instance of its own and to use TP's instead.

Not covered here: DCP < TP (e.g. TP8/DCP4), which should take the dedicated-instance path unchanged.

**Update (2026-10-18): the hang is node-specific and does not reproduce with this PR on other nodes.** Both hangs happened on one node (pit2-p03-g10). On two other MI355X nodes, the same image, recipe and PR ran clean for several hours, with the same throughput as without the PR. We no longer attribute the hang to this PR. The original report is kept below for reference.

**Results (all c60 / max-num-seqs 120, same image, recipe and PR commit)**

| node | PR | run | outcome |

<details>
<summary>Original report (2026-10-17), superseded by the update above</summary>

Stress test results with the AgentX workload: with this PR we see a reproducible all-rank hang at higher concurrency. The same setup without the PR runs clean.

**Setup**
- MI355X x8, Kimi-K3 FP4, TP8 / DCP8, `dcp_comm_backend=a2a`, DSpark spec decode (4 tokens, synthetic acceptance length 3.36)
- `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (CPU KV offload), `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraphs, `max-num-batched-tokens 8192`
- `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=0`, so the query gather goes through this PR's path (log: `Using AITER custom all-gather for the MLA DCP query.`)
- Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294` (aiter 0.1.25), PR applied at `8033f2c`
- AgentX trace replay (`semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`), 1 h measured run after warmup

**Hang signature on g10** (identical on both tries)
- Engine throughput drops to 0 with about 55–60 running requests, while CPU-offload KV loads are in flight.
- About 600 s later, every rank (0–7) times out on the same NCCL all-gather:
  ```
  Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=21277, OpType=_ALLGATHER_BASE, NumelIn=5529600, NumelOut=44236800, Timeout(ms)=600000)
  ```
  (try 1: `SeqNum=326677, NumelIn=4755456`)
- `NumelIn` is exactly `num_tokens x 12 heads x 576` (800 and 688 tokens), which matches the DCP query gather. In bf16 that is above the `should_custom_ag` limit (8 MiB per rank, about 606 tokens), so it is this PR's NCCL fallback inside `_aiter_query_gather`.

**Possible mechanism (hypothesis, not confirmed)**
- With the PR, the DCP group alternates between AITER `allgather_lastdim` (small batches, cudagraph decode) and NCCL `all_gather` (large mixed-prefill batches).
- One rank's GPU stream may have been blocked by an earlier AITER custom kernel still spinning in `start_sync`/`end_sync`. For reference, ROCm/aiter#4786 (open) changes the cross-device flag loads in `start_sync`/`end_sync` from `DEVICE` to `SYSTEM` scope. aiter 0.1.25 in this image still uses `DEVICE`.

**Review note:** the DCP direct workspaces are allocated per ubatch (`num_ubatches`), but the new AITER instance on the DCP group (one signal buffer, one staging buffer) is shared. With ubatch overlap enabled, two concurrent query gathers could use the same instance. That was not enabled in our runs.

</details>
